newsitem.title: JAPAN: Major Japanese bank reported to be in merger deal.
newsitem.headline: Major Japanese bank reported to be in merger deal.

text.p: Japan's Hokkaido Takushoku Bank, the country's tenth-largest commercial bank, has agreed to merge with a smaller regional bank, domestic news reports said late Monday.

The bank will merge with the smaller Hokkaido Bank Ltd, the reports said, with the new entity focussing on becoming a regional powerhouse on Japan's northernmost main island. Both banks are headquartered in the Hokkaido city of Sapporo.

A senior official with Japan's Ministry of Finance, which supervises the banking sector, said he was aware the two banks were in merger discussions but said he could not confirm that a deal had been reached.
The agreement was reported by the Jiji and Kyodo news agencies, quoting informed sources. They said an announcement would be made on Tuesday.
Hokkaido Takushoku has long been rumoured to be a merger candidate given its heavy burden of problem loans.
A wave of such mergers is expected to hit the troubled banking sector in Japan as it braces for the "Big Bang" financial reforms planned by the Japanese government.
The industry has been plagued by problem loans after the collapse of Japan's real estate bubble in the early 1990s.

According to the Ministry of Finance, Japan's deposit-taking financial institutions had 29 trillion yen ($233 billion) worth of problem loans at the end of last September. But many analysts say the true size is twice to three times the official figure.

Jiji said that as part of the merger, Hokkaido Takushoku would end its international operations and focus on domestic business. It said that both banks would restructure their Tokyo operations and close overlapping branches in Hokkaido.
The reports gave no further details of the merger agreement and the two banks were not available for comment.
